correctness.rationale: For any map the exact affine-period subspace T determines AddInd=q/|T| by linear extension. For a cyclotomic map H stabilizes T under scalar multiplication; with index <=p, necessarily |H|>(q/p), forcing T=0 or all of Fq. If T=Fq, root counting of a reduced linearized polynomial against its monomial restriction on H forces a single Frobenius term. At index p+1, x+c x^p over F_{p^2}, with norm(c) !=1, is invertible and non-Frobenius but additive-index 1. Exact independent F9 finite enumeration corroborates and does not substitute for proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating paper proposes a tradeoff between additive and multiplicative indices and proves only AddInd>=p in the low-cyclotomic-index case. The maximal AddInd=p^n result for every extension degree, together with an explicit sharp boundary at p+1, is a complete structural classification of the first low-index regime, not a routine value calculation. No general higher-index theorem is asserted.
